item.title: Macklem says U.S. trade unpredictability could set back recent economic progress
item.description: Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem says the unpredictability of U.S. trade policy could set back the recent progress by the Canadian economy.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: HALIFAX — Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem says the unpredictability of U.S. trade policy has increased uncertainty and could set back the recent progress by the Canadian economy. In prepared remarks for a speech in Halifax, Macklem says the changing trade picture could cause businesses to delay investment and hiring decisions. He says that if new U.S. tariffs remain in place, the rate of growth for the economy could be roughly halved in the fourth quarter to below one per cent. The trade challenges come as Macklem says the war in the Middle East pushes oil and gasoline prices higher. He says as things stand now, if oil prices stay near US$100 per barrel, the central bank would expect inflation to edge up in the coming months. Macklem says the bank has been looking through the direct impact of higher oil prices on inflation so far, but the risk that it becomes more persistent has increased. --- This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 21, 2026.

item.title: CAE nabs $300M contract with U.S. air force despite Trump's Canadian procurement ban
item.description: CAE Inc. says it has secured a $300-million contract to train U.S. air force crews, despite Trump's ban on procurement from Canadian companies.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: MONTREAL — CAE Inc. says it has secured a $300-million contract to continue training U.S. air force crews, even as U.S. President Donald Trump has moved to ban Canadian companies from government procurement. The Montreal-based flight simulator maker says the deal granted to its American defence division extends CAE’s role as the main contractor schooling U.S. aircrews on the C-130 Hercules military transport plane, a role it has played since 2018. CAE says training of pilots, flight engineers and navigators will take place at air force bases in Little Rock, Ark., as well as Georgia, Wyoming, Minnesota and Missouri through 2035. The announcement comes in spite of a decree from Trump on Sept. 16 that bans the federal government from procuring Canadian items. It remains unclear whether the presidential order covers services, rather than goods alone, or whether Canadian companies with U.S. subsidiaries fall under the ban. The move last week marked the latest escalation of the trade war between Canada and the United States after negotiations between the two countries broke down last month. --- This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 21, 2026.

item.title: Irving Oil names Alfred Stern, former CEO of Austria's OMV, as next president and CEO
item.description: Irving Oil has announced the appointment of European energy executive Alfred Stern as its next president and chief executive.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: SAINT JOHN — Irving Oil has announced the appointment of European energy executive Alfred Stern as its next president and chief executive. The New Brunswick company says Stern will join Irving on Oct. 1 and assume the top job effective Nov. 1, following the retirement of Jeff Matthews. Stern most recently served as chairman and chief executive of Austrian oil and gas group OMV AG. In a statement, Stern says he is honoured to join Irving Oil team at such an “important time in its history.” He says he plans to build on the company’s strong foundation by investing in safety, reliability and security of supply to support Irving Oil’s long-term, sustainable growth. Irving Oil, a privately owned energy company based in Saint John, N.B., operates the largest oil refinery in Canada, with capacity of more than 320,000 barrels per day. --- This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 21, 2026.

Security selection is key and would advise investors to select securities that are inexpensive and have identifiable catalysts. The company is evaluating ten newly identified oil prospects at approximately 1,500 metres.
